text.p: - Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek visited Slovenia's only nuclear power plant Krsko over the weekend.
- Government said 95 percent of border disputes between Slovenia and Croatia are solved, but local inhabitants claim the figure is much lower.
- Two local communities from northwestern Slovenia, Bovec and Kranjska Gora, joined international ecological project CIPRE which encompasses 26 Alpine communities from seven countries.
- A Slovenian on average consumes 215 litres of milk per year, making the nation one of the lowest consumers of milk in Europe, experts say.
- Slovenia will soon have a new archbishop as the current archbishop, Alojzij Sustar, offered his retirement to the Pope due to his 75 years of age.
- General elections scheduled for November 10 will cost the country's budget 410 million tolars ($2.9 million).
- The Slovenian distributor of electrical power -- Eles -- said its investment this year will total some three billion tolars ($21.9 million).
